text: And afterward it will come to pass that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
Even on the male and female servants I will pour out my Spirit in those days.

versions.text: Even on the servants and the maidservants I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pairs עֲבָדִים with שְׁפָחוֹת (male and female slaves/servants). 'Servants and maidservants' obscures the deliberate pairing and sounds uneven when read aloud.

text: I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.

versions.text: I will set signs in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מוֹפְתִים denotes 'wonders' or 'portents' rather than the more neutral 'signs' (אוֹתוֹת). 'Show wonders' also reads more naturally aloud than 'set signs.'

text: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.

And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has said, even among the survivors whom the LORD calls.

versions.text: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has said, among the survivors whom the LORD calls.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew begins the final clause with the conjunction (וּבַשְּׂרִידִים); rendering it 'even among the survivors' preserves the connective and gives the closing line a smoother cadence for oral reading.
